timeline.cite: [I-M] the archive's own reading. NO ANNAL DATES THIS REMOVAL. Grey Annals §132 (year header 422) does grant Brethil by Thingol's leave — 'Here at the prayer of Inglor Thingol granted to Haleth's people to live in Brethil' — BUT CHRISTOPHER TOLKIEN DISQUALIFIES IT FOR THIS RECORD IN HIS OWN WORDS: 'Haleth here is of course Haleth the Hunter, who had entered Beleriand two years before' (HoME XI, commentary on Of the Coming of Men into the West §29). The Lady Haleth's Haladin do not occur in the Grey Annals text at all — 'Haladin' 0 times. The only dates are TYPED MARGINS on the LQ 1 typescript: the stockade siege 375, the Estolad sojourn 376–390, the crossing of the Brithiach 391, Haleth's death 420. AND 390 IS THE END OF THE SOJOURN, NOT THE REMOVAL — the crossing is margined 391, and Thingol's grace carries no date at all. The strictest true statement is: after 391, not later than 420, dated by nothing
